subject: EDA InsightLab Apex browser statistics engine

findings.title: Exact-source extraction is fingerprint-locked
findings.claim: The verifier executes selected functions extracted from the supplied Apex app.js rather than a rewritten statistical implementation.
findings.evidence: Node and Python independently hashed the same source; SHA-256 a15f8c9830c2729392e02e54abe2c62a3caba885b08f3aba8b575d522a2ef395.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hash in every published report and fail closed when extraction anchors change.

findings.title: Core numeric primitives agree with reference libraries
findings.claim: Linear quartiles, sample standard deviation, and pairwise-complete Pearson correlation should match NumPy-compatible definitions.
findings.evidence: Functions begin near app.js lines 447, 460, and 472.
findings.recommendation: Promote these checks into permanent regression tests with boundary, constant-vector, and non-finite cases.

findings.title: Skewness uses a nonstandard mixed estimator
findings.claim: A displayed skewness value needs a named estimator and should agree with a documented statistical convention.
findings.evidence: The implementation near app.js line 465 matches neither tested SciPy convention.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document one estimator (for example adjusted Fisher-Pearson), add golden cases, and label the UI definition.

findings.title: Quoted CSV fields survive commas, escaped quotes, and embedded newlines
findings.claim: The local CSV parser should preserve common quoted-field semantics.
findings.evidence: Exercised the exact parser beginning near app.js line 398.
findings.recommendation: Retain this as a regression fixture and add BOM, CR-only, blank-header, and malformed-quote cases.

findings.title: Duplicate CSV headers silently overwrite data
findings.claim: Every input field should remain addressable or ingestion should reject an ambiguous schema.

acceptable_behaviour: deterministically rename to measure and measure_2

findings.evidence: The parsed row contains only one measure key with value 2; the first value is lost without an error.
findings.recommendation: Validate header uniqueness before row materialization and emit a structured, row-independent schema error or deterministic renaming map.

findings.title: High-cardinality numeric identifiers are inferred as measurements
findings.claim: Identifier inference should not depend on a column being nonnumeric; integer keys must be protected from correlations, scaling, feature ranking, and PCA.
findings.evidence: The identifier branch near app.js line 501 excludes already inferred numeric columns.
findings.recommendation: Add semantic key heuristics plus an explicit user override; never place high-cardinality numeric keys into PCA by default.

findings.title: Duplicate and IQR diagnostic counts match the declared rules
findings.claim: Exact-row duplicate counting and linear-quartile 1.5×IQR flags should be independently reproducible.
findings.evidence: Computed through computeProfile beginning near app.js line 515.
findings.recommendation: Add fixtures that distinguish row count, distinct duplicate groups, and extra copies; name the quartile interpolation method in documentation.

findings.title: Eta-squared group separation matches the reference decomposition
findings.claim: Numeric-predictor versus categorical-target relevance should equal between-group sum of squares divided by total sum of squares.
findings.recommendation: Add missing groups, single-level targets, imbalanced groups, and invariance under label renaming.

findings.title: Low-cardinality Cramer's V matches the uncorrected definition
findings.claim: For complete low-cardinality tables, Apex should match the explicitly documented raw Cramer's V formula.
findings.evidence: The implementation near app.js line 1926 uses sqrt(chi2 / (n * min(r-1,c-1))) without finite-sample correction.
findings.recommendation: Label the statistic as uncorrected Cramer's V and optionally expose a bias-corrected mode for small or wide tables.

findings.title: Cramer's V changes when rows are reordered
findings.claim: A categorical association statistic must be invariant to row order.
findings.evidence: Encounter-order level truncation changes which categories enter the contingency calculation.
findings.recommendation: Reject unsupported cardinality or collapse levels deterministically by frequency with an explicit other bucket; never truncate by encounter order.

findings.title: Categorical predictors are not target-aware for numeric outcomes
findings.claim: A target-aware ranker should distinguish a categorical feature that separates a numeric target from an equally cardinal but uninformative feature.

reference.suggested_measure: eta-squared with numeric target grouped by categorical predictor

findings.evidence: Both features receive the same unique-ratio fallback even though signal partitions low versus high target values.
findings.recommendation: Implement numeric-target-by-categorical-predictor relevance (eta-squared/ANOVA or cross-validated univariate models) and test permutation sensitivity.

findings.title: Leakage guard depends on naming or recorded feature lineage
findings.claim: An exact raw copy of the target under an unrelated name should be surfaced as a leakage hazard rather than recommended as a predictor.

reference.expected: flag exact/near target proxy for review or exclusion

findings.evidence: isTargetDerivedColumn near app.js line 1682 checks naming and recorded engineered-feature source text, not value identity.
findings.recommendation: Add exact/near-duplicate target checks, suspicious post-outcome feature rules, and provenance-aware leakage diagnostics; keep human review mandatory.

findings.title: PCA explained-variance ratios agree on complete numeric data
findings.claim: Power iteration plus rank-one deflation should reproduce a full-SVD PCA oracle on a well-conditioned complete matrix.
findings.evidence: computePCA begins near app.js line 2010 and uses 80 fixed power iterations.
findings.recommendation: Retain full-SVD differential tests and add repeated-eigenvalue, ill-conditioned, sparse, and convergence-residual cases.

findings.title: PCA silently ignores numeric predictors after the first ten
findings.claim: The PCA result should enumerate all exclusions and must not imply that it represents the full numeric predictor space when columns were silently capped.

reference.expected: all eligible columns or a visible deterministic selection policy

findings.recommendation: Remove the cap for ordinary browser-sized data or expose the cap, selection order, and excluded columns in the UI and exported report.

findings.title: PCA missing-value scaling differs from an impute-then-scale pipeline
findings.claim: Missing-value handling before PCA needs an explicit, reproducible operation order.
findings.evidence: standardizedMatrix substitutes zero for missing standardized values while scaling from pre-imputation summaries.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document a pipeline order; for modeling, fit imputation and scaling on training data only and export those fitted parameters.

findings.title: Missing-token policy is deterministic but domain-sensitive
findings.claim: String sentinels should be configurable because tokens such as '-' may be legitimate categorical values.

reference.expected_product_behaviour: publish and permit override of missing-token vocabulary

findings.evidence: isMissing near app.js line 383 hardcodes the sentinel set.
findings.recommendation: Display the active sentinel policy at import, support per-column overrides, and record it in pipeline JSON.
